new_candidates.date_enacted: 2026-07-21 (City Council adopted Resolution 26-R-042 by a 9-0 vote)
new_candidates.duration: 8 months from adoption, or until City Council takes final action on comprehensive plan amendment PLN-COMP-2026-002, whichever occurs first
new_candidates.legal_basis: Resolution 26-R-042, adopted by Chesapeake City Council 9-0 on July 21, 2026
new_candidates.trigger: Council sought to pause discretionary review of data center land-use applications while comprehensive plan amendment PLN-COMP-2026-002 is pending
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of the July 31, 2026 research date. The resolution temporarily defers Planning Commission recommendations and City Council consideration of discretionary land-use applications (e.g., rezonings, conditional use permits) for proposed data centers, for 8 months from adoption (to approximately 2027-03-21) or until Council takes final action on PLN-COMP-2026-002, whichever occurs first. It does not stop administrative or by-right processing.
new_candidates.affected_projects: No single named project; applies citywide to discretionary data center land-use applications pending before the Planning Commission or City Council.
new_candidates.outcome: Enacted deferral of discretionary data center land-use applications pending completion of a related comprehensive plan amendment.

evidence.title: Chesapeake City Council meeting minutes/clip, July 21, 2026
evidence.supports: Council adopted Resolution 26-R-042 by a 9-0 vote on July 21, 2026, deferring discretionary data center land-use applications for 8 months or until final action on PLN-COMP-2026-002, whichever is first.

evidence.title: Chesapeake City Council places hold on data center applications
evidence.supports: Describes the scope of the resolution as a temporary hold on discretionary data center applications rather than a blanket construction or permit ban.

new_candidates.notes: Virginia localities generally lack a general moratorium power, and this action is structured as a deferral of discretionary applications tied to a pending comprehensive plan amendment rather than an outright application freeze, consistent with the state note on Virginia's narrow local authority. Three other events tagged 'Moratorium vote' in the same chronology sweep were reviewed and rejected as candidates: Suffolk (2026-06-17) only directed the Planning Commission to draft a permanent citywide prohibition, with no numbered instrument enacted; Front Royal (2026-06-23) rejected an enabling zoning amendment and directed staff to prepare moratorium language within 60 days, again with no enacted ordinance located; Loudoun County (2026-07-22) explicitly directed staff only to research the legality and scope of a possible pause, with the chronology stating no moratorium or processing pause was enacted by that vote.
